subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should external plugins receive synchronous fail-closed authority over every persisted OpenClaw config mutation, and if so what recovery and scope limits must the shared mutation layer enforce?
rationale: This creates a new public plugin API and delegates control over security-sensitive persisted configuration, so code inspection cannot choose fail-open behavior, recovery bypasses, or which writers are covered without maintainer intent.

options.title: Shared bounded veto hook
options.body: Add a typed pre-commit hook in the shared mutation layer after built-in validation, with timeouts, redaction, deterministic ordering, and an operator-controlled recovery bypass.

options.title: Gateway RPC-only policy
options.body: Limit interception to config.set, config.patch, and config.apply, accepting that CLI, doctor, onboarding, and plugin-originated writes remain outside the contract.

options.title: Keep validation core-owned
options.body: Do not grant plugin veto authority; continue adding generic built-in validation and protected-path rules while external validators remain advisory.

recommendation.title: Shared bounded veto hook
recommendation.body: Add a typed pre-commit hook in the shared mutation layer after built-in validation, with timeouts, redaction, deterministic ordering, and an operator-controlled recovery bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history across both the shared config mutation path and plugin hook contract, and the discussion already routes the decision to maintainer follow-up.
